name: mid-fullstack-remote-us
note: Four years full-stack, dense with real metrics, against a US remote product engineer posting on the same stack. Strong match and should score high. The risk here is inflation, not fabrication: the numbers are already good.
resume_text:
Daniel Okonkwo
Full-Stack Engineer | Austin, TX (Remote) | d.okonkwo@example.com | (512) 555-0148
github.com/dokonkwo | danielokonkwo.dev

SUMMARY
Full-stack engineer, four years, mostly on small teams where the person who writes the API
also writes the screen that consumes it and carries the pager for both.

EXPERIENCE

Halcyon Health - Software Engineer
Remote (HQ Denver, CO) | Mar 2023 - Present
- Owned the patient intake service end to end: a TypeScript and Node.js API behind
  Postgres, serving 40k intake submissions a month across 180 clinics.
- Cut p95 intake submission latency from 2.4s to 610ms by replacing three sequential
  lookups with a single joined query and adding two covering indexes.
- Rebuilt the intake form in React with react-hook-form and Zod, dropping validation-related
  support tickets from roughly 60 a month to under 10.
- Moved 14 background jobs off cron into BullMQ with retries and a dead letter queue,
  ending a class of silent failures that had gone unnoticed for two months.
- Wrote the migration that split the monolithic appointments table, executed in four
  batched steps with zero downtime on a 38 million row table.
- Set up Playwright end-to-end coverage for the five flows that generate revenue. Caught
  nine regressions before release in the first quarter.
- Mentored two engineers through their first six months, including their first on-call
  rotations.

Rivermark Logistics - Software Engineer
Austin, TX | Jul 2021 - Feb 2023
- Built the carrier rate comparison feature in React and Redux Toolkit, used by 900 daily
  active dispatchers.
- Integrated four carrier APIs behind one internal interface, so adding the fifth took two
  days instead of the three weeks the first had taken.
- Reduced the main bundle from 1.8MB to 740KB with route level code splitting and by
  replacing moment with date-fns.
- Added Sentry and structured logging, which took mean time to identify production errors
  from around a day to under an hour.

PROJECTS
shipcalc - github.com/dokonkwo/shipcalc
- An open-source freight rate calculator in TypeScript. 340 stars, 11 contributors.

EDUCATION
B.S. Computer Science, University of Texas at Austin, 2017 - 2021

SKILLS
Languages: TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, SQL
Frontend: React, Redux Toolkit, Next.js, Tailwind CSS, react-hook-form, Playwright
Backend: Node.js, Express, Fastify, PostgreSQL, Prisma, Redis, BullMQ
Infrastructure: AWS (ECS, RDS, S3, CloudWatch), Docker, Terraform, GitHub Actions
Other: REST, GraphQL, Sentry, Datadog
jd_text:
Product Engineer, Full-Stack
Remote (United States) | Engineering | $145,000 - $175,000 + equity

Vessel is a 34 person company building operations software for specialty healthcare
practices. We are profitable, we are not raising, and we ship to production several times a
day. Engineering is 11 people across four timezones, all US.

We are hiring a product engineer. That means you will not be handed a spec. You will talk to
the clinics that use the product, decide with your PM what is worth building, build the API
and the interface, and own it after it ships.

You will
- Design and build features across the stack: TypeScript everywhere, React on the front,
  Node.js and Postgres on the back
- Own data modelling decisions and write your own migrations, including the awkward ones on
  large tables where downtime is not an option
- Instrument what you ship. We expect you to know whether the thing you built is working
  without waiting for a support ticket to tell you
- Carry a one-week pager rotation roughly every two months
- Review other people's code carefully and take review on your own without defensiveness

We are looking for
- 3 to 6 years writing production software, with real ownership of at least one service or
  surface rather than tickets across many
- Strong TypeScript. Not "I have used it", but a working sense of what the type system is
  and is not doing for you
- React in production, with an understanding of rendering behaviour and state management
  beyond reaching for a library
- Postgres: schema design, indexes, query plans, and the judgement to read one before
  guessing
- Background job processing and the failure modes that come with it
- Experience with end-to-end or integration testing that people actually keep running
- Comfort in a remote-first company: you write things down, and you unblock yourself

Bonus, genuinely not required
- AWS or another cloud at the level of owning your own infrastructure
- Terraform or comparable infrastructure as code
- Healthcare, HIPAA, or another regulated domain
- Open-source work we can read
- Having mentored someone

How we interview
A 30 minute conversation, a 90 minute paid work session on a problem from our real backlog,
a systems conversation, and a call with the founders. Four hours of your time total. We give
a decision within three business days of the last round.

Benefits: full medical, dental and vision for you and dependents, 4 weeks PTO with a
2 week minimum we enforce, $3,000 annual equipment budget, twice yearly company offsite.
